set.typical_award_size: NOFA issued October 23, 2025 for $7,960,000 ($4,650,000 former RDA LMIHF plus $3,310,000 Affordable Housing Impact Fees), with about $5.8 million in expected Elco Yards (1601 El Camino Real) housing impact fees added. Two applications. Redwood City Pulse reported Council approval on May 11, 2026. Separate Affordable Housing Preservation Program: over-the-counter gap loans to convert market-rate units to deed-restricted units or preserve expiring restrictions; first project 417 Stambaugh Street (8 units, about $1.2 million loan, June 2025); about $5.8 million remained in HPP funds; guideline amendments were on the May 11, 2026 agenda.
set.per_unit_cap: NOFA guidelines limit RDA LMIHF and impact fee subsidy to $200,000 per City-regulated unit; Council raised the limit to $300,000 per unit for the 2026 awards (the City regulates no more than 49% of units to stay outside Article 34). HOME funds follow HUD per-unit limits.
set.affordability_requirement: New construction multifamily rental of 5 or more units; all City-funded units at or below 80% AMI and at least 15% of units at or below 30% AMI (extra points for more extremely low income units); 55-year City regulatory agreement (HOME units also carry the 20-year HOME term).
set.next_deadline: No open round as of November 8, 2026. The last NOFA was issued October 23, 2025 and awarded May 11, 2026; no new NOFA appears on City Council agendas through November 9, 2026. Preservation Program is over the counter.

set.layering_notes: County layer: every San Mateo County city project competes for the County Affordable Housing Fund NOFA (AHF 14 closed July 15, 2026, next fall 2027), HEART bridge loans and HACSM project-based vouchers; city money is usually the first commitment that unlocks those. Reclassified from other to loan: the fund has deployable money and records loan repayment income ($514,717 in FY 2025-26), so it lends to affordable projects, and the five-year plan programs $4,000,000 to Housing Land Purchase (CIP 310416). After the $1,000,000 Bespoke set-aside and the $4,000,000 land purchase, only about $0.3 million of the $5,292,314 ending balance is unprogrammed, so new requests depend on future fee receipts. Pair a request with the County AHF NOFA. The City is a CDBG entitlement and joins the County HOME Consortium. Source is the FY 2025-26 Mitigation Fee Act (AB 1600) annual report; fee rates confirmed in the FY 2026-27 Comprehensive Fee Schedule.

set.typical_award_size: Requirement, not a subsidy. Residential developments of 5 or more units: for-sale projects provide 20% of units at moderate income; rental projects provide 10% at low income (rents at 30% of 70% AMI). On-site units required at 15 or more for-sale units and 20 or more rental units; smaller projects pay the Required In Lieu Fee. Rental developers may instead elect the Alternative In Lieu Fee, and rental projects over 50 units may combine on-site units (at least half the requirement or 5% of units) with Required In Lieu Fees. Fees per square foot of livable space (Resolution 18-174, November 26, 2018, as posted by the City): Required In Lieu Fee $45 ownership and $35 rental; Alternative In Lieu Fee $48 (rental only). Projects approved before July 1, 2018 pay the older Affordable Housing Impact Fee ($21 to $35 per square foot after February 1, 2020). Fees go to the Affordable Housing Trust Fund, which the City uses with state and HUD funds for 100% affordable projects (Daly City is a CDBG and HOME entitlement city).
set.next_deadline: Applies at entitlement; Alternative In Lieu Fees are due in full at building permit issuance. In-lieu fees are set by Council resolution (current posted schedule is Resolution 18-174). Daly City is a participant in the 2026 multi-city nexus study.
